source: Klein & Wright (2016) Macrocognition: From Theory to Toolbox
finding: History of NDM then macrocognition then tools. The recognition-primed decision (RPD) model was the founding result that answered the charge that nothing useful comes from field study of decisions.
numbers: RPD accounted for 80-90% of firefighter decisions (Klein et al. 1986). It depended on 10-20 years of experience. Replications named: military leaders (Schmitt & Klein 1999), firefighters (Keren et al. 2013), offshore oil platform managers (Skriver 1998); tests by Klein et al. 1995 and Johnson & Raab 2003.
quote: The RPD model accounted for 80-90% of the decisions that firefighters made.
limits: Written by the founders. The 80-90% figure is a coder classification of reported decisions, not a measured outcome gain. Replications are mostly other field studies using the same interview method.
agent_relevance: A scaffold that forces option comparison everywhere contradicts the finding that experts often match a pattern and test one option by simulation. Keep a fast single-option path with a check.

source: Klein & Wright (2016) Macrocognition: From Theory to Toolbox
finding: Lab critics reacted strongly. Lipshitz et al. (2001) asked NDM to add rigorous controlled methods; 16 commentaries followed. NDM answered that controlled tests would stop it being NDM. Earlier, 'naturalistic memory' was attacked in 1989 and faded; NDM did not.
numbers: Lipshitz et al. 2001, J Behavioral Decision Making: 1 target article, 16 commentaries. 12 NDM conferences held by 2016.
limits: Account of the dispute comes from one side. No head-to-head test of RPD against rival models is reported in this paper.
agent_relevance: Keep our evidence rule two-sided: field description finds the phenomenon, a controlled test measures its size. Treat NDM claims as hypotheses to measure on our benchmarks.

source: Klein & Wright (2016) Macrocognition: From Theory to Toolbox
finding: Seven beliefs the NDM/macrocognition view says it overturned: options must be compared; expertise is rules; goals must be clear first; sensemaking builds up from data; insight needs breaking mental sets; more information cuts uncertainty; teaching critical-thinking steps such as listing assumptions improves performance.
numbers: Sources cited for 'more data hurts': Cannon-Bowers 1993, Omodei 2005, Flin 2008, Grossman 2014. For 'listing assumptions fails': Klein 2011, Stanton 2011, Hoffman 2014. No effect sizes given.
limits: Claims by the school, backed by field cases. Effect sizes are not shown here.
agent_relevance: Fits guardrails G1 and G2: no assumption-listing or doubt on a schedule; rethink on a real signal. Still test it ourselves, since no effect sizes are given.

source: Klein & Wright (2016) Macrocognition: From Theory to Toolbox
finding: Tool-stage examples: a field study of signals passed at danger found the cause was display design (a red light always on, signals hidden behind long trains), not driver inattention. A 2-day cognitive task analysis workshop for community health workers was called highly successful.
numbers: No effect sizes given. Cases: Multer et al. 2015; Safar et al. 2015; Holtrop et al. 2015.
limits: Case-level success claims. No control group is described.
agent_relevance: When the agent fails, look for a fault in the frame or in what counted as data before blaming effort. Matches the data-frame view.

source: Klein & Wright (2016) Macrocognition: From Theory to Toolbox
finding: Macrocognition is defined by what it studies, not by a separate mechanism: decisions, sensemaking, planning, coordination and expertise under time pressure, uncertainty and teams. It admits it studies tasks with no correct answer, so performance is hard to score.
numbers: Micro versus macro: working memory and attention versus decisions in complex work.
quote: It is less concerned with precision than with plausibility.
limits: Self-described weakness. It is the main reason evidence here is weaker than in lab fields.
agent_relevance: Our agent works on tasks with a checker, so we can do what macrocognition cannot: measure. Use its constructs as hypotheses, not proof.

source: Ward, Hoffman, Conway et al. (2017) Editorial: Macrocognition, the science and engineering of sociotechnical work systems (reporting Collins et al.)
finding: Editorial of the Frontiers Research Topic. Reports that sports coaches use deliberation as a check on initial intuitions, which are heavily shaped by prior planning and experience.
numbers: No sample sizes in the editorial.
limits: Second-hand summary; I did not read Collins et al. itself.
agent_relevance: Supports a design where a fast first answer gets a cheap check, not a long debate.

source: Ward et al. (2017) Frontiers editorial (reporting Brouwers et al., rail control cue utilization)
finding: Reports that in a simulated rail control task, people with greater cue utilization routed trains more effectively while managing extra load.
numbers: Direction only; no numbers in the editorial.
limits: Second-hand. A measured size from a related cue-utilization study is in the 2019 control-room line below.
agent_relevance: Cue utilization (spotting diagnostic features fast) is a trainable skill. Check the agent's feature-picking step, not only its reasoning.

source: Ward et al. (2017) Frontiers editorial (reporting Buchler et al.)
finding: Reports that sending many messages can decrease the likelihood of attaining shared situation awareness. Similar function and similar initial awareness among members probably shaped this.
numbers: Full numbers are in the Buchler 2016 line.
limits: Second-hand.
agent_relevance: More messages between agents, or more context into one agent, can hurt. Add a relevance filter.

source: Ward et al. (2017) Frontiers editorial (reporting Porat et al.)
finding: Reports experienced operators supervised about 15 unmanned systems at moderate automation but controlled only up to three effectively; teams generally beat individuals.
numbers: 15 supervise, 3 control.
limits: Second-hand; detail is in the Porat 2016 line.
agent_relevance: Supervision and hands-on control have different capacity limits. Code should supervise; the model should control one thing at a time.

source: Ward et al. (2017) Frontiers editorial (reporting Laurent & Bianchi)
finding: A critical paper in the topic asks whether macrocognition should be distinguished from other cognition and proposes a multiscale model.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Theory critique, not data.
agent_relevance: Do not treat macro versus micro as two mechanisms. Our schema can use macro functions as labels over the same operators.

source: Laurent & Bianchi (2016) Macrocognition through the Multiscale Enaction Model: a blind spot of macrocognition
finding: Macrocognition's interests (complexity, goal competition, cognitive-affective and social interaction, situatedness) are real, but the authors say it should not be set apart epistemologically from cognition and call for one multiscale model.
numbers: No empirical sample. Opens with Bruner & Goodman (1947): lab laws stay valid but describe the market place poorly.
limits: Theory paper. Only the opening was read closely.
agent_relevance: A competing framing: scale matters, mechanism does not. Fits keeping one schema and varying the context.

source: Buchler, Hoffman, Lazarus et al. (2016) Mission command in the age of network-enabled operations: social network analysis of information sharing and situation awareness
finding: Tested the network-enabled-operations assumption that more information sharing raises situation awareness (SA). In a 2-week military exercise, people who sent more email had lower SA. Higher SA went with a lower chance of out-ties.
numbers: Email network: 213 staff, 19,168 messages. Phone network: 3,191 calls among 132 staff. SA survey of core units; 89 nodes in the models (exponential random graph models). A few people held most ties (Pareto pattern). Ties formed mainly among people with the same function and similar SA (homophily).
quote: increased email output was associated with lower individual situation awareness
limits: One exercise, observational, SA from self-report survey. Causal direction unclear: low-SA people may simply send more.
agent_relevance: Strong boundary condition: broadcasting is not coordination. In multi-agent setups, share on request or on a signal, not by default.

source: Porat, Oron-Gilad, Rottem-Hovev, Silbiger (2016) Supervising and controlling unmanned systems: a multi-phase study with subject matter experts
finding: Studies with expert operators. One experienced operator can supervise up to 15 UAS at moderate automation and control up to 3. Beyond that, teams did better, except when tasks were similar or areas overlapped, where one operator beat a team that had to coordinate.
numbers: Supervise about 15 (Study 1 reached 15 to 17 only on a limited mission component); control 3. After a health-display redesign, fault-source detection fell from an average of 13 min to under 5 min in 95% of cases. 3-UAS task: multiple reporting of the same vehicle 25% for team versus 8% for a single operator with toolkit.
limits: Small expert samples, simulated missions, design-research method. Many contrasts have no inferential statistics.
agent_relevance: Coordination has a cost: splitting work among agents wins only when tasks differ. Matches our finding that same-model voters are correlated (G4).

source: Klein, Mitchell, Hoffman et al. (2023) The plausibility transition model for sensemaking
finding: Sensemaking as story building: a surprise triggers a story, each step is a state transition judged for plausibility, gaps cause strain, and the loop ends when plausibility is enough. Gaps are closed by gathering data, doubting the data, adding assumptions, or elaborating the story.
numbers: Built from 23 cases chosen from a convenience corpus of 73 (Klein et al. 2021): e.g. Air France 447, USS Vincennes, Royal Majesty grounding, AlphaGo.
limits: One reviewer (the senior author) coded the cases. No inter-rater check and no test of predictions. Authors call it an initial exploration.
agent_relevance: A candidate state sequence for impasse handling: code detects surprise, build a causal chain, locate the weakest transition. Test against our impasse detector before adding.

source: Klein, Mitchell, Hoffman et al. (2023) The plausibility transition model for sensemaking
finding: Anomaly detection is not outlier detection: an anomaly is noticed when an expectation is violated. Stories can oversimplify when causes intersect.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Stated by the authors as a limitation of sequential stories.
agent_relevance: A statistical outlier flag is not enough for the impasse detector; it needs an explicit expectation to violate (for example predicted output from the draft).

source: Jalaeian, Morey, Rayo (2025) Joint activity design heuristics for enhancing human-machine collaboration
finding: Fourteen heuristics for joint human-machine work, grouped by five macrocognitive functions: event detection, sensemaking, adaptability, perspective shifting, coordination. Revised after practitioner feedback.
numbers: Round 1: 8 practitioners, 5 designs. Round 2: 13 practitioners (1 to 25 years experience), each rated 2 technologies on a 1-5 scale per heuristic. Thematic analysis only.
limits: No outcome measure and no comparison group. It shows practitioners can apply it, not that designs improve.
agent_relevance: A review checklist for agent tool design, unproven. Do not count as evidence of gain.

source: Kahneman & Klein (2009) Conditions for intuitive expertise: a failure to disagree
finding: Opponents (heuristics-and-biases versus NDM) agree on the discriminating test: trust intuition only if the environment is regular enough to be predictable and the person had a chance to learn it. Felt confidence is not a reliable sign of accuracy.
numbers: Position paper; no sample. Only the abstract was read, via the Europe PMC record.
quote: Subjective experience is not a reliable indicator of judgment accuracy.
limits: Abstract only; full text not opened. Agreement is between two named authors, not a community.
agent_relevance: Design rule: trust a fast answer according to environment validity (is there a checker, is the task regular), not the model's stated confidence.

source: Naturalistic decision-making in sport: how current advances into the recognition-primed decision model offer insights (2022)
finding: Review of RPD in sport. In Macquet's (2020) review 60-81% of expert decisions were simple match, 13-28% diagnosis, 3-24% course-of-action evaluation. Players far from the ball had time to simulate; rugby coaches under less time pressure deliberated more.
numbers: Share of decisions by RPD level as given. Studies span football, volleyball, handball, hockey, judo, rugby.
limits: Mostly qualitative interview studies. The authors say consistent empirical evidence for an intuitive-to-analytic continuum in sport is lacking.
agent_relevance: Time pressure shifts the mix: more time, more simulation. A budgeted agent could set how much checking to run from its time budget.

source: Naturalistic decision-making in sport (2022)
finding: RPD evidence in sport rests mostly on after-the-event interviews. The review lists open paradoxes and asks for work on how cues are selected.
numbers: Many qualitative studies (volleyball, soccer, badminton, judo, hockey), no controlled effect sizes quoted.
limits: Retrospective interviews can reconstruct a pattern story that was not the real process. This is the core weakness of RPD evidence.
agent_relevance: Ties to our rule that written reasoning is not a reliable record of how the model decided.

source: Control room operators' cue utilization predicts cognitive resource consumption during regular operational tasks (2019)
finding: Power-grid control operators were grouped by a cue-utilization test battery. The lower-cue group showed larger rises in prefrontal oxygenation on regular work than the higher-cue group, with no difference in rated workload.
numbers: About 35 operators. Session 1: F(1,33) about 5, p=.029, eta-squared=.136. Session 2: F(1,33) about 4, p=.038, eta-squared=.123. Multivariate effect on rated workload not significant (eta-squared about .013). Cue group did not differ in years in the job.
limits: Small N, two groups clustered from the same sample, forehead sensor only. Experience years did not separate the groups.
agent_relevance: Skill at pattern recognition is separable from time served. Agent equivalent: measure whether the first-features step finds the diagnostic cues; reasoning length does not show it.

source: Vaccaro, Almaatouq, Malone (2024) When combinations of humans and AI are useful: a systematic review and meta-analysis
finding: Across 106 experiments, human+AI teams did worse than the best of human alone or AI alone. Decision tasks lost; content-creation tasks gained, not significantly. Teams gained when the human was better than the AI and lost when the AI was better.
numbers: 106 studies, 370 effect sizes. Overall Hedges g = -0.23 (95% CI -0.39 to -0.07). Decision tasks g = -0.27 (CI -0.44 to -0.10, P=.002). Creation tasks g = +0.19 (CI -0.09 to 0.48, P=.18, n=34). Task-type moderator F(1,104)=7.84, P=.006.
quote: human–AI combinations performed significantly worse than the best of humans or AI alone
limits: Studies from Jan 2020 to June 2023, possible publication bias, mixed samples (doctors, crowd workers, students). Excludes tasks neither can do alone.
agent_relevance: Joint-system claims need testing: on a checkable decision, a human override of a stronger model can lower accuracy. Let code arbitrate.

source: Toward a science of human-AI teaming for decision making: a complementarity framework (2026)
finding: Framework paper: complementarity needs role partition, calibrated trust, shared mental models and training. Says meta-analyses show hybrid teams can beat either alone, but only when collaboration is well calibrated.
numbers: No new data. Cites the Vaccaro 2024 meta-analysis, a 2016 trust-and-team-performance meta-analysis and a qualitative meta-analysis of hybrid performance.
limits: Conceptual. Its summary is more hopeful than Vaccaro's own average result (g = -0.23).
agent_relevance: Read the original meta-analysis, not the summary.

source: Increasing large language model accuracy for care-seeking advice using prompts reflecting human reasoning strategies (2026)
finding: Direct test of NDM prompts on LLMs. Recognition-primed and data-frame prompts raised accuracy on 45 patient vignettes (3 urgency levels) over a default prompt, mostly on self-care cases.
numbers: 10 ChatGPT models x 3 prompts x 45 vignettes x 10 runs = 13,500 assessments. Accuracy: default 63.3% (CI 61.9-64.7), recognition-primed 67.6% (CI 66.3-69), data-frame 66.7% (CI 65.3-68). Odds ratios 2.26 (z=8.69) and 2.05 (z=7.23), both P<.001. Self-care: 13.4% to 29.8% (recognition-primed) and 24.6% (data-frame). Largest model gain: GPT-4.1 mini +13 points with data-frame.
limits: One task and domain. Only 2 emergency cases. Only ChatGPT-family models. Prompts add reasoning tokens, so cost rises. Not a clinical validation.
agent_relevance: Best direct evidence that macrocognitive prompts help an LLM, but the gain is about 4 points and confounded with extra reasoning text. Treat as a lead and run a length-matched control.

source: Increasing LLM accuracy for care-seeking advice using NDM prompts (2026), per-case and per-model detail
finding: The prompt effect is uneven: it helps some cases, hurts others, and did not help the newest models.
numbers: Recognition-primed prompt raised accuracy in 18 of 45 cases (40%) and lowered it in 13 (29%); median gain 18% (IQR 5-24%), median loss 5%. GPT-4.1 self-care went from 0% to 43.8%. GPT-5.2 Instant 57.8 to 56.4 and GPT-5.2 Thinking 52.0 to 53.1 (no gain). 92% of the drops were in nonemergency cases. Over-triage was 88% of all errors. Reasoning models gained more (OR 2.15 vs 1.70 for nonreasoning, recognition-primed).
limits: Per-model confidence intervals are about plus or minus 4-5 points and overlap for many models.
agent_relevance: The prompt mainly shifted the answer prior (more self-care answers). That may be a base-rate shift, not better reasoning. Check for it before crediting the method.

source: Mainali et al. (2025) Classical AI vs. LLMs for decision-maker alignment in health insurance choices
finding: A classical system built on case-based reasoning, Bayes and NDM, and zero-shot LLM decision makers (GPT-4, GPT-5, weighted self-consistency), matched target decision makers about equally.
numbers: Overall alignment accuracy: classical 0.892, GPT-5 0.895, GPT-4 0.892. Targets at risk tolerance 0.0, 0.5, 1.0; LLMs near perfect at the extremes, dropped at 0.5 where the classical system stayed steadier.
limits: One dataset, three target profiles, no confidence intervals. Differences of 0.003 are noise.
agent_relevance: Prompts struggle to describe a middle setting; language cannot cleanly separate it from the extremes. Be wary of persona voting for mid-range cases.

source: Kostka & Chudziak (2025) Towards cognitive synergy in LLM-based multi-agent systems: integrating theory of mind and critical evaluation
finding: A multi-agent LLM system on one strategic business decision. Theory of mind plus a critic agent scored best on LLM-judged quality.
numbers: Base system: argument quality 2.75, critical engagement 0.00, risk resolution 0%. Both modules: 3.43, 0.38, 48.75%. Critic-only risk resolution 22.5%. Neither module alone guaranteed high performance. Scored by an LLM judge.
limits: One case study, LLM judge with no expert validation (authors admit), no statistics, high self-preference risk.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence and the judge is not independent of the agents. Do not adopt a critic agent on this; our G2 demands revision from real output.

source: Alacam et al. (2026) Modeling student sensemaking with LLMs and knowledge-graph-guided inference (listing only)
finding: Seen only as a title in an arXiv search listing. Not used as evidence.
numbers: None read.
limits: Title only.
agent_relevance: Check later if sensemaking measures are needed.

source: To advance translational science, remove these roadblocks to studying team knowledge integration (2025)
finding: Many 'interdisciplinary' teams are not: experts are listed together but work as parallel play or handoffs. The National Academies team-science report says not all recommended practices work for every team.
numbers: No data in this commentary.
limits: Opinion piece; names boundary conditions without measuring them.
agent_relevance: Check that multi-agent runs really integrate each other's outputs and are not parallel samples with a vote.

source: Jagpal et al. (2024) Beyond the individual: a multidisciplinary model for critical thinking in the ICU
finding: Splits micro (individual thinking in a controlled setting), macro (real environment) and team cognition. Says team cognition can improve diagnostic accuracy, but offers a teaching model, not data.
numbers: No sample or effect size.
limits: Educator model with a case example; the accuracy claim is not backed here.
agent_relevance: Adds no evidence. Do not count it as support for team scaffolds.
